description: Comprehensive question bank derived from Karnataka Geography study material (Sections 3.6.1-3.6.27). All questions verified against source PDF. Covers location, physiography, rivers, dams, climate, soils, forests, wildlife, agriculture, irrigation, minerals, industries, transport, population, urban geography, energy, environmental problems, and district profiles.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Where is Karnataka located in India?

options.B: West-central part of peninsular India on the Deccan Plateau
options.C: Southern tip of the Indian subcontinent

questions.explanation: Karnataka lies in the west-central part of peninsular India, mainly on the Deccan Plateau, with an Arabian Sea coastline in the west.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the approximate latitudinal extent of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: A commonly used approximate extent is 11°31'N to 18°45'N latitude. Some official documents round this to about 11.5°-18.5°N.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the approximate longitudinal extent of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The approximate longitudinal extent is 74°12'E to 78°35'E. Some documents round this to 74°-78.5°E.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the total geographical area of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The current Survey of India / India State of Forest Report figure is about 191,791 km².

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is Karnataka's rank among Indian states by geographical area?
questions.explanation: Karnataka is the sixth-largest Indian state by area, after Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Does the Tropic of Cancer pass through Karnataka?

options.C: No, it lies entirely north of Karnataka

questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer (23°30'N) lies entirely north of Karnataka. Karnataka lies wholly in tropical latitudes south of the Tropic of Cancer.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which state borders Karnataka to the north?
questions.explanation: Karnataka shares a land boundary with Maharashtra to the north.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which state borders Karnataka to the northwest?
questions.explanation: Goa borders Karnataka to the northwest.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which state borders Karnataka to the northeast?
questions.explanation: Telangana borders Karnataka to the northeast.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which state borders Karnataka to the east?
questions.explanation: Andhra Pradesh borders Karnataka to the east.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which state borders Karnataka to the southeast?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu borders Karnataka to the southeast.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which state borders Karnataka to the southwest?
questions.explanation: Kerala borders Karnataka to the southwest.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the revised coastline length of Karnataka as per the 2025 Survey of India re-verification?
questions.explanation: The re-verified Survey of India coastline figure promulgated in 2025 is 343.30 km. Older books commonly quote approximately 300-320 km.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: How many revenue divisions does Karnataka have?
questions.explanation: Karnataka has four revenue divisions: Bengaluru, Mysuru, Belagavi and Kalaburagi.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is the headquarters of the Belagavi revenue division?
questions.explanation: Belagavi is the headquarters of the Belagavi revenue division.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is the headquarters of the Kalaburagi revenue division?
questions.explanation: Kalaburagi is the headquarters of the Kalaburagi revenue division.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: How many districts does Karnataka have as per the 2026 Local Government Directory listing?
questions.explanation: The Government of India's Local Government Directory listing updated in 2026 shows 31 districts. Vijayanagara was created in 2021 and Ramanagara was renamed Bengaluru South in 2025.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Ramanagara district was renamed as:
questions.explanation: Ramanagara district was renamed Bengaluru South on 23 May 2025. Ramanagara remains its headquarters.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Vijayanagara district was created in 2021 by bifurcating which district?
questions.explanation: Vijayanagara was created in 2021 by bifurcating Ballari district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are the three major physiographic divisions of Karnataka?

options.B: Coastal Plain (Karavali), Western Ghats (Malnad), Maidan (Deccan Plateau)
options.D: Northern Plains, Central Highlands, Southern Plateau

questions.explanation: The common broad division is (1) Coastal Plain or Karavali, (2) Western Ghats / Malnad, and (3) Maidan or Deccan Plateau.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the difference between Malnad and Maidan?

options.A: Malnad is dry plateau, Maidan is wet hills
options.B: Malnad is elevated wet hill country, Maidan is drier open plateau east of the Ghats
options.C: Malnad is coastal plain, Maidan is Western Ghats

questions.explanation: Malnad is the elevated, dissected and wetter hill country associated with the Western Ghats. Maidan is the plateau and plain country east of the Ghats, generally drier and more open.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: The Coastal Karnataka region (Karavali) is characterized by:

options.B: Narrow low-lying plain with humid climate and high monsoon rainfall
options.D: Rolling plains with red loamy soils

questions.explanation: Karavali is a narrow, low-lying coastal plain between the Arabian Sea and Western Ghats with humid, very high monsoon rainfall and lateritic and alluvial soils.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: The Northern Maidan region is characterized by:

options.B: Semi-arid to sub-humid climate with extensive black cotton soils

questions.explanation: The Northern Maidan is a broad, comparatively dry plateau with rolling plains and isolated hills, semi-arid to sub-humid climate, extensive black cotton soils in basaltic tracts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: The Western Ghats in Karnataka are also known as:
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats are also known as the Sahyadri range.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the highest peak in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Mullayanagiri in the Chandra Drona range of Chikkamagaluru district, about 1,930 m above sea level, is the highest peak in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Mullayanagiri peak is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Mullayanagiri is located in the Chandra Drona range of Chikkamagaluru district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the approximate height of Mullayanagiri?
questions.explanation: Mullayanagiri is approximately 1,930 m above sea level.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is the highest peak in Kodagu district?
questions.explanation: Tadiandamol is the highest peak in Kodagu district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Baba Budangiri is located in which hill range?
questions.explanation: Baba Budangiri is in the Chandra Drona hill range in Chikkamagaluru district. It is associated with Dattatreya Peetha.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Kudremukh is known for:

options.B: National park, iron-ore mining history, rolling grasslands

questions.explanation: Kudremukh in Chikkamagaluru region is a prominent grassland-forest massif with a national park and iron-ore mining history.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Pushpagiri / Kumara Parvatha is located in which region?
questions.explanation: Pushpagiri / Kumara Parvatha is in the Kodagu-Dakshina Kannada border region and is an important peak and wildlife sanctuary landscape.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Brahmagiri hill range is located on the border of Karnataka and:
questions.explanation: Brahmagiri is a hill range on the Karnataka-Kerala border in the Talakaveri region of Kodagu.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Nandi Hills is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Nandi Hills is a historic hill station near Bengaluru in Chikkaballapura district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Biligiriranga Hills (BRT) is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Biligiriranga Hills is in Chamarajanagar district and is an ecological link between the Eastern and Western Ghats.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Male Mahadeshwara Hills is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Male Mahadeshwara Hills is a forest hill range and wildlife landscape in Chamarajanagar district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Chamundi Hills overlooks which city?
questions.explanation: Chamundi Hills is a prominent isolated hill overlooking Mysuru.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Savandurga is known for:
questions.explanation: Savandurga in Bengaluru South region is a large granite monolith/hill complex.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Kodachadri peak is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Kodachadri is a Western Ghats peak in Shivamogga district near the Mookambika landscape.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Kemmangundi hill station is located in which range?
questions.explanation: Kemmangundi is a hill station in the Baba Budan range in Chikkamagaluru district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Yana in Uttara Kannada is known for:
questions.explanation: Yana is known for distinctive limestone/karst rock pinnacles, not a high mountain peak.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Charmadi Ghat connects the Dakshina Kannada coast with:
questions.explanation: Charmadi Ghat connects the Dakshina Kannada coast with the Chikkamagaluru interior.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Shiradi Ghat links the Mangaluru region with:
questions.explanation: Shiradi Ghat links the Mangaluru region with Hassan.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Agumbe Ghat links coastal Udupi/Shivamogga-side routes with:
questions.explanation: Agumbe Ghat links coastal Udupi/Shivamogga-side routes with the Malnad region.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Bisle Ghat is a forested pass in which region?
questions.explanation: Bisle Ghat is a forested pass in the Sakleshpur-Subrahmanya region.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Hulikal Ghat links coastal and Malnad routes in which region?
questions.explanation: Hulikal Ghat links coastal and Malnad routes in the Shivamogga-Udupi region.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Why does the Western Ghats receive heavy rainfall?

options.B: Due to orographic uplift of southwest monsoon winds

questions.explanation: Most southwestern monsoon winds from the Arabian Sea are forced to rise over the Ghats. Orographic uplift cools the air, causing condensation and heavy windward rainfall.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: The plateau east of the Western Ghats crest lies partly in:
questions.explanation: The plateau east of the crest lies partly in a rain shadow because descending air is drier and rainfall is reduced.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: When was the Western Ghats inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List?
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats serial property was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2012.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of endemic wildlife of the Western Ghats?
questions.explanation: The lion-tailed macaque is an example of endemic Western Ghats wildlife, along with the purple frog, Nilgiri tahr in the wider Ghats, and numerous endemic amphibians.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is a major conservation concern in the Western Ghats?

options.B: Habitat fragmentation due to road and rail expansion

questions.explanation: Habitat fragmentation, road and rail expansion, dams, quarrying and mining, plantation expansion, invasive species, tourism pressure, fires, landslides and climate change threaten ecological integrity.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are the Deccan Traps?

options.B: Extensive flood-basalt lava flows formed around the end-Cretaceous period

questions.explanation: The Deccan Traps are extensive flood-basalt lava flows, mainly in Maharashtra and adjoining regions, formed around the end-Cretaceous period. The term 'trap' refers to step-like topography.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Basalt weathering has produced extensive ________ soils in suitable areas.
questions.explanation: Basalt weathering has produced extensive black cotton soils in suitable areas.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which rock formation is important for gold, iron and manganese mineralisation in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Dharwar schist belts are important for gold, iron and manganese mineralisation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which are the three coastal districts of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The three coastal districts are Uttara Kannada, Udupi and Dakshina Kannada.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Maravanthe is noted for:

options.B: A road between the Arabian Sea and the Souparnika River

questions.explanation: Maravanthe is noted for the road between the Arabian Sea and the Souparnika River.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is Karnataka's major all-weather port?
questions.explanation: New Mangalore Port at Panambur is Karnataka's major all-weather port and a major port under the Union government.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Karwar is important as:
questions.explanation: Karwar is a naval harbour and port in Uttara Kannada district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a west-flowing river of coastal Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Sharavathi is an important west-flowing river. Other west-flowing rivers include Kali, Gangavali, Aghanashini, Varahi, Sita, Swarna and Netravati.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the importance of mangroves in coastal Karnataka?

options.B: They stabilise shorelines, trap sediment, store carbon and provide nursery habitat
options.C: They are used for gold mining
options.D: They are a source of black soil

questions.explanation: Mangroves stabilise shorelines, trap sediment, store carbon, provide nursery habitat for fish and crustaceans, and reduce wave energy.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Why do Karnataka's rivers flow in both directions?

options.B: Because the Western Ghats form a major watershed

questions.explanation: The Western Ghats form a major watershed. Short, swift rivers descend westward to the Arabian Sea, while longer rivers flow east across the plateau towards the Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Where does the Krishna River originate?

options.B: Near Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats of Maharashtra

questions.explanation: The Krishna rises near Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats of Maharashtra and flows east/southeast through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Where does the Kaveri River originate?

options.C: Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Kodagu

questions.explanation: The Kaveri originates at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Kodagu district, Western Ghats.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Tunga and Bhadra rivers meet at Koodli to form which river?
questions.explanation: Tunga and Bhadra meet near Koodli in Shivamogga district to form the Tungabhadra.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is a major tributary of the Krishna River relevant to Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Important tributaries of the Krishna relevant to Karnataka include Bhima, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha and Tungabhadra.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: The Bhima River originates in the Bhimashankar region of Maharashtra and joins the Krishna in:
questions.explanation: The Bhima originates in the Bhimashankar region of Maharashtra and joins the Krishna in Telangana.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which tributary of the Krishna is associated with the Hidkal dam and Gokak Falls?
questions.explanation: The Ghataprabha flows eastward through the Belagavi/Bagalkote region. Hidkal dam is on the Ghataprabha and Gokak Falls is on this river.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Navilaitirha/Renuka Sagar dam is on which river?
questions.explanation: Navilaitirha/Renuka Sagar is on the Malaprabha River in Belagavi district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is a major tributary of the Kaveri in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Major tributaries of the Kaveri in Karnataka include Hemavati, Harangi, Lakshmana Tirtha, Kabini, Shimsha, Arkavathi and Suvarnavathi.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: The Kabini River originates in the Wayanad highlands of Kerala and joins the Kaveri at:
questions.explanation: The Kabini joins the Kaveri at T. Narasipura. The Kabini reservoir is near H D Kote.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: The Hemavati River originates in the Western Ghats of Chikkamagaluru district and joins the Kaveri near:
questions.explanation: The Hemavati joins the Kaveri near the KR Nagar region. The Gorur/Hemavati reservoir is on this river.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: The Arkavathi River originates in the Nandi Hills region and joins the Kaveri near:
questions.explanation: The Arkavathi originates in the Nandi Hills region and joins the Kaveri near Kanakapura. Hesaraghatta/Thippagondanahalli system is associated with it.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: The Kaveri water dispute concerns sharing of waters among which states?

options.B: Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry

questions.explanation: The dispute concerns sharing of Kaveri waters among Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry. The Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal gave its final award in 2007; the Supreme Court modified allocations in 2018.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which body oversees implementation of the Kaveri water sharing arrangements?

options.B: Cauvery Water Management Authority and Cauvery Water Regulation Committee

questions.explanation: The Cauvery Water Management Authority and Cauvery Water Regulation Committee oversee implementation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: The Mekedatu proposal is:

options.B: A contested proposed balancing reservoir and drinking-water/hydropower project

questions.explanation: The Mekedatu proposal is a contested proposed balancing reservoir and drinking-water/hydropower project, not an existing completed dam.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which part of Karnataka drains into the Godavari system?

options.B: Northeastern part through tributaries like Manjira

questions.explanation: Only the northeastern part of Karnataka drains into the Godavari system, chiefly through tributaries such as the Manjira in the Bidar-Kalaburagi region. The main Godavari channel does not flow through Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: The Manjira River is a tributary of:
questions.explanation: The Manjira is an important tributary of the Godavari, rising in Maharashtra and flowing through parts of Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a west-flowing river of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Aghanashini is a west-flowing river in Uttara Kannada. Important west-flowing rivers include Kali, Gangavali, Aghanashini, Sharavathi, Varahi, Chakra, Sita, Swarna and Netravati.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Jog Falls is formed by which river?
questions.explanation: Jog Falls is on the Sharavathi River in Shivamogga district, with four main cascades: Raja, Rani, Roarer and Rocket.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: The Sharavathi River is associated with which reservoir?
questions.explanation: Linganamakki reservoir is on the Sharavathi River in Shivamogga district and is a major reservoir for Sharavathi hydropower.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Supa, Kadra and Kodasalli projects are on which river?
questions.explanation: Supa, Kadra and Kodasalli projects are on the Kali River in Uttara Kannada district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: The Netravati River flows through which district before joining the Gurupura near Mangaluru?
questions.explanation: The Netravati originates in the Chikkamagaluru/Kodagu highlands and flows through Dakshina Kannada, joining the Gurupura near Mangaluru.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the difference between a river mouth, estuary and delta?

options.B: River mouth is where a river enters a water body; estuary is a tidal brackish river mouth; delta is a depositional landform at a river mouth
options.C: Estuary is a mountain, delta is a plateau
options.D: Delta is a type of estuary

questions.explanation: A river mouth is the point where a river enters a receiving water body. An estuary is a tidal, brackish river mouth where freshwater mixes with seawater. A delta is a depositional landform built where sediment accumulates at a river mouth.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is the largest major river basin in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Krishna basin covers a large part of northern Karnataka and is the largest major river basin in the state.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an east-flowing river basin of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The major east-flowing basins are Krishna, Kaveri, Godavari, Pennar and Palar. West-flowing basins include Kali, Sharavathi, Aghanashini, Bedti/Gangavali, Varahi and Netravati.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Groundwater availability in hard-rock Karnataka is strongly controlled by:
questions.explanation: In hard-rock Karnataka, groundwater availability is strongly controlled by weathering depth and fractures.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which regions of Karnataka are drought-prone?

options.B: Parts of North Interior Karnataka and rain-shadow districts

questions.explanation: Drought risk is high in parts of North Interior Karnataka and the rain-shadow districts of the southern and central plateau, including areas of Vijayapura, Bagalkote, Koppal, Raichur, Ballari, Chitradurga, Kolar and Chikkaballapura.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which regions of Karnataka are flood-prone?

options.B: Krishna-Tungabhadra basin, coastal rivers and urban catchments

questions.explanation: Flood risk is significant along the Krishna and its tributaries in northern districts, the Tungabhadra basin, and low-lying coastal and Malnad river valleys during intense monsoon rainfall.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is watershed management?

options.B: Integrated planning of land, water and vegetation within a catchment to reduce runoff and erosion

questions.explanation: Watershed management is integrated planning of land, water and vegetation within a catchment to reduce runoff and erosion, increase infiltration and recharge, improve soil moisture and sustain livelihoods.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS) dam is built on which river?
questions.explanation: KRS dam is on the Kaveri River near Srirangapatna in Mandya district. It is associated with Brindavan Gardens.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Almatti / Lal Bahadur Shastri Dam is built across which river?
questions.explanation: Almatti / Lal Bahadur Shastri Dam is on the Krishna River in Vijayapura district and is part of the Upper Krishna Project.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Narayanapura / Basava Sagar dam is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Narayanapura / Basava Sagar is on the Krishna River in Yadgir district and is part of the Upper Krishna Project.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Tungabhadra Dam is located near which town?
questions.explanation: Tungabhadra Dam is near Hosapete in Vijayanagara district and supports irrigation and power.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Bhadra Dam is located at Lakkavalli in which district?
questions.explanation: Bhadra Dam is at Lakkavalli in Chikkamagaluru district on the Bhadra River, supporting irrigation and power.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Hidkal dam is on which river?
questions.explanation: Hidkal dam is on the Ghataprabha River in Belagavi district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Hemavati / Gorur reservoir is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Hemavati / Gorur reservoir is on the Hemavati River in Hassan district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Harangi reservoir is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Harangi reservoir is on the Harangi River in Kodagu district, part of the Kaveri basin.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Kabini reservoir is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Kabini reservoir is near H D Kote in Mysuru district, part of the Kaveri basin.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Markonahalli dam is on which river?
questions.explanation: Markonahalli dam is on the Shimsha River in Tumakuru district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Yagachi dam is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Yagachi dam is on the Yagachi River in Hassan district for irrigation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Manchanabele dam is on which river?
questions.explanation: Manchanabele dam is on the Arkavathi River in Bengaluru Rural / Bengaluru South region for water supply and irrigation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Jog Falls is formed by which river?
questions.explanation: Jog Falls is on the Sharavathi River in Shivamogga district, with four main cascades: Raja, Rani, Roarer and Rocket.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are the four main cascades of Jog Falls?
questions.explanation: Jog Falls has four main cascades: Raja, Rani, Roarer and Rocket.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Gokak Falls is on which river?
questions.explanation: Gokak Falls is on the Ghataprabha River in Belagavi district. It has a horseshoe-like fall and historic power-generation association.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Shivanasamudra falls is on which river?
questions.explanation: Shivanasamudra falls is on the Kaveri River in the Mandya-Chamarajanagar region. It has Gaganachukki and Bharachukki falls and an early hydroelectric station.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which are the two falls at Shivanasamudra?
questions.explanation: Shivanasamudra has Gaganachukki and Bharachukki falls.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Abbey Falls is located near which town?
questions.explanation: Abbey Falls is near Madikeri in Kodagu district on a Kaveri tributary stream.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Hebbe Falls is located in which region?
questions.explanation: Hebbe Falls is a two-tier fall in the Kemmangundi area of Chikkamagaluru district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Unchalli / Lushington Falls is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Unchalli / Lushington Falls is a high waterfall in a forested valley in Uttara Kannada district on an Aghanashini tributary.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Magod Falls is on which river system?
questions.explanation: Magod Falls is on the Bedti/Gangavali system in Uttara Kannada district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Sathodi Falls is in which district?
questions.explanation: Sathodi Falls is a scenic forest waterfall in Uttara Kannada district on a local stream in the Kali basin.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Barkana Falls is on which river?
questions.explanation: Barkana Falls is on the Sita River in Shivamogga district near the Agumbe region.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Kunchikal Falls is on which river?
questions.explanation: Kunchikal Falls is on the Varahi River in Shivamogga district. It is commonly cited as Karnataka's highest waterfall by total height.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Chunchanakatte Falls is on which river?
questions.explanation: Chunchanakatte Falls is a Kaveri cascade in Mysuru district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Godchinamalaki Falls is on which river?
questions.explanation: Godchinamalaki Falls is on the Markandeya River in Belagavi district and is also called Markandeya Falls.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which waterfall is commonly cited as the highest in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Kunchikal Falls is commonly cited as Karnataka's highest waterfall by total height, though published height and ranking depend on measurement method and seasonal flow. Jog Falls is the best-known major waterfall.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What type of climate does Karnataka have?
questions.explanation: Karnataka has a predominantly tropical monsoon climate, modified by altitude, distance from the sea, relief and seasonal wind patterns.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which monsoon branch gives Karnataka most of its rainfall?

options.A: Bay of Bengal branch of northeast monsoon
options.B: Arabian Sea branch of southwest monsoon

questions.explanation: The Arabian Sea branch of the southwest monsoon is the principal source of rainfall for the coast and Western Ghats.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are the main seasons of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: A practical climatological division is summer/pre-monsoon (March-May), southwest monsoon (June-September), post-monsoon/northeast monsoon (October-December), and winter (January-February).

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is a rain-shadow region?

options.B: A leeward area where descending air is drier and rainfall is reduced

questions.explanation: A rain-shadow region lies on the leeward side of a mountain barrier where descending air is drier and rainfall is reduced. Much of the interior plateau east of the Western Ghats is in a rain-shadow influence.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which are climate hazards of Karnataka?

options.B: Drought, floods, landslides, heatwaves, coastal erosion

questions.explanation: Drought, intense rainfall, flash floods, river floods, landslides in Ghats, heatwaves, coastal erosion and changing monsoon variability are important hazards.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is Karnataka's average annual rainfall (1961-2010 normal)?
questions.explanation: The 1961-2010 state normal in a Karnataka disaster-management plan is about 1,153 mm. A commonly used long-term state average is approximately 1,150 mm.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which region of Karnataka receives the highest rainfall?

options.B: Coastal Karnataka and windward Western Ghats

questions.explanation: The coastal belt and windward Western Ghats receive the highest rainfall. Udupi, Dakshina Kannada, Uttara Kannada, Kodagu, Shivamogga and Chikkamagaluru highlands contain very wet pockets.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which region of Karnataka generally receives the lowest rainfall?

options.B: Parts of northern interior and leeward central/southeastern plateau

questions.explanation: The lowest rainfall generally occurs in parts of the northern interior and leeward central/southeastern plateau. District-wide averages conceal large taluk-level differences.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the approximate annual rainfall of Coastal Karnataka (1961-2010 normal)?
questions.explanation: Coastal Karnataka has an approximate annual rainfall of 3,518 mm (1961-2010 normal), the highest regional normal.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the approximate annual rainfall of Malnad (1961-2010 normal)?
questions.explanation: Malnad has an approximate annual rainfall of 1,950 mm (1961-2010 normal) due to high orographic rainfall.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the approximate annual rainfall of South Interior Karnataka (1961-2010 normal)?
questions.explanation: South Interior Karnataka has an approximate annual rainfall of 714 mm (1961-2010 normal).

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the approximate annual rainfall of North Interior Karnataka (1961-2010 normal)?
questions.explanation: North Interior Karnataka has an approximate annual rainfall of 702 mm (1961-2010 normal) and is generally dry and drought-prone.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which agency operates dense automatic weather/rainfall observations in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre (KSNDMC) operates and disseminates dense automatic weather/rainfall observations, including district, taluk and hobli-level data.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which soil is commonly associated with basaltic regions of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Basalt weathering commonly forms clay-rich black soil (regur) in northern Karnataka's basaltic tracts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which soil is widespread in the southern and eastern plateau of Karnataka, coloured by iron oxides?
questions.explanation: Red soil is widespread in the southern and eastern plateau; iron oxides give red colour; often light-textured and low in organic matter.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Laterite soil is commonly found in which regions of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Laterite soil occurs in high-rainfall Ghats and coastal uplands; intense leaching makes it iron/aluminium-rich. It suits cashew, arecanut and plantations with suitable soil amendments.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Alluvial soils in Karnataka are found in:

options.A: River valleys, floodplains and coastal deposits

questions.explanation: Alluvial soils occur in river valleys, floodplains and coastal deposits with variable texture and fertility. They suit paddy, sugarcane, vegetables and other irrigated crops.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: How are Karnataka soils formed?

options.B: Through weathering of parent rocks influenced by climate, relief, organisms, time and drainage

questions.explanation: Soils develop through weathering of parent rocks under the influence of climate, relief, organisms, time and drainage. Basalt yields black soils; granite-gneiss contributes red and lateritic soils; river deposition produces alluvial soils.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What causes soil erosion and degradation in Karnataka?

options.B: Deforestation, overgrazing, cultivation along steep slopes, intense runoff, mining and construction

questions.explanation: Deforestation, overgrazing, cultivation along steep slopes, intense runoff, mining, construction, wind erosion, salinity and nutrient depletion degrade soil.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which crops are suitable for black soil in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Black soil is clay-rich with high moisture retention and suits cotton, jowar, pulses and oilseeds. Drainage and cracking management are concerns.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which crops are suitable for red soil in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Red soil is often light-textured and low in organic matter. It suits ragi, groundnut, pulses, millets and horticulture with nutrient and moisture management.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Coastal sandy soils in Karnataka are suitable for which crops?

options.B: Coconut and cashew in suitable sites

questions.explanation: Coastal sandy soils are sandy, often saline-influenced coastal strips. Coconut and cashew suit suitable sites, but nutrient and water retention are limitations.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which forest type is found in the very wet Western Ghats and coastal slopes of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Tropical evergreen forests occur in very wet Western Ghats and coastal slopes with species like Dipterocarpus, Cullenia and Myristica swamps with dense multi-layer canopy.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which forest type is found in the Malnad and wetter interior belts of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Moist deciduous forests occur in Malnad and wetter interior belts with teak, rosewood, Terminalia and bamboo in suitable tracts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which forest type is found in the interior plateau and eastern slopes of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Dry deciduous forests occur in the interior plateau and eastern slopes with teak in some tracts, sandalwood, Anogeissus, Dalbergia and bamboo.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which forest type is found in dry northern and southeastern districts of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Thorn/scrub forests occur in dry northern and southeastern districts with Acacia, thorny shrubs and drought-adapted grasses.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Montane shola/grassland vegetation is found in which region of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Montane shola/grassland occurs in high-altitude Ghats with patches of stunted evergreen shola and grassland.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Mangrove vegetation in Karnataka is found in:
questions.explanation: Mangroves occur in estuaries and tidal creeks with Avicennia, Rhizophora and associated salt-tolerant plants.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which tree species is strongly associated with Karnataka's heritage and forest economy?
questions.explanation: Sandalwood is strongly associated with Karnataka's heritage and forest economy, though its availability and trade are regulated.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the difference between forest cover and tree cover?

options.B: Forest cover meets FSI canopy-density and minimum-area definition irrespective of ownership; tree cover includes smaller patches and scattered trees
options.C: Tree cover is larger than forest cover
options.D: Forest cover only includes government forests

questions.explanation: Forest cover is land meeting the Forest Survey of India canopy-density and minimum-area definition, irrespective of legal ownership or land use. Tree cover includes smaller patches and scattered trees outside the mapped forest-cover definition.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is social forestry?

options.A: Planting trees in reserved forests only
options.B: Tree planting and management with community participation for local needs and environmental benefits

questions.explanation: Social forestry involves tree planting and management with community participation for local needs and environmental benefits.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the difference between afforestation and reforestation?

options.B: Afforestation establishes tree cover on land not recently forested; reforestation restores forest on previously forested land
options.D: Reforestation is in coastal areas only

questions.explanation: Afforestation establishes tree cover on land not recently forested; reforestation restores forest on previously forested land. Deforestation is conversion or removal of forest cover.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is a national park in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The principal national parks are Bandipur, Nagarahole (Rajiv Gandhi), Bannerghatta, Kudremukh and Anshi (now within the Kali Tiger Reserve landscape).

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Bandipur National Park / Tiger Reserve is located in which districts?
questions.explanation: Bandipur National Park / Tiger Reserve is in Chamarajanagar and Mysuru districts. It is known for tiger and elephant and is part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve landscape.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Nagarahole (Rajiv Gandhi) National Park is located in which districts?
questions.explanation: Nagarahole (Rajiv Gandhi) National Park / Tiger Reserve is in Kodagu and Mysuru districts. It is connected to Wayanad and Bandipur landscapes.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Bannerghatta National Park is located near which city?
questions.explanation: Bannerghatta National Park is in the Bengaluru Urban region, near metropolitan Bengaluru, with southern dry forest and a biological park.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Kudremukh National Park is located in which region?

options.A: Chikkamagaluru, Udupi and Dakshina Kannada region

questions.explanation: Kudremukh National Park is in the Chikkamagaluru, Udupi and Dakshina Kannada region with Western Ghats evergreen forest, shola-grassland and endemic biodiversity.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Anshi National Park is now within which tiger reserve landscape?
questions.explanation: Anshi National Park is now within the Kali Tiger Reserve landscape in Uttara Kannada district, with evergreen forest, Kali river landscape and tiger habitat.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: How many tiger reserves does Karnataka have according to NTCA?
questions.explanation: The National Tiger Conservation Authority lists five tiger reserves in Karnataka: Bandipur, Bhadra, Biligiri Ranganatha (BRT), Kali and Nagarahole.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a tiger reserve of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The five tiger reserves are Bandipur, Bhadra, BRT, Kali and Nagarahole. Bannerghatta is a national park, not a tiger reserve.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which are Ramsar wetlands in Karnataka?

options.A: Ranganathittu, Ankasamudra, Aghanashini Estuary, Magadi Kere
options.B: KRS reservoir, Unkal Lake, Hesaraghatta tank

questions.explanation: Karnataka's designated Ramsar sites include Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary, Ankasamudra Bird Conservation Reserve, Aghanashini Estuary and Magadi Kere Conservation Reserve.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary is a designated:
questions.explanation: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary is a designated Ramsar wetland in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve was designated under UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere Programme in which year?
questions.explanation: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve was designated under UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere Programme in 1986. It spans parts of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which Karnataka forest landscapes are part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve?
questions.explanation: Karnataka components of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve include important forest landscapes such as Bandipur and Nagarahole.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is an example of endemic or threatened wildlife associated with Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Examples include lion-tailed macaque, Nilgiri langur, Malabar giant squirrel, tiger, Asian elephant, dhole, gaur, sloth bear, great hornbill and endemic Western Ghats amphibians and reptiles.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are conservation reserves and community reserves?

options.B: Protected-area categories under the Wildlife (Protection) Act

questions.explanation: Conservation reserves and community reserves are protected-area categories under the Wildlife (Protection) Act. Conservation reserves are generally government-owned areas; community reserves involve community or private lands with local community participation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are the main agricultural seasons in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Kharif crops are sown with the southwest monsoon (June-July); Rabi crops are sown after the monsoon; Zaid refers to short summer-season crops.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Coffee cultivation in Karnataka is concentrated in which districts?
questions.explanation: Kodagu, Chikkamagaluru and Hassan are the principal coffee-growing districts. Arabica and Robusta are cultivated under shade in the Western Ghats highlands.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which crops are important in northern Karnataka?

options.B: Jowar, tur, Bengal gram, cotton, sunflower, safflower, soybean

questions.explanation: Jowar, tur, Bengal gram, cotton, sunflower, safflower, soybean, sugarcane in irrigated tracts, grapes and pomegranate are important in northern Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which crops are important in coastal and Malnad Karnataka?

options.B: Rice, arecanut, coconut, cashew, pepper, cardamom, coffee, ginger, turmeric

questions.explanation: Rice, arecanut, coconut, cashew, pepper, cardamom, coffee, ginger and turmeric are important in coastal and Malnad Karnataka due to high rainfall and humid conditions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Is apple a major commercial crop of Karnataka?

options.B: No, most of the state lacks cool temperate conditions needed for conventional apple production

questions.explanation: Apple is not a major commercial crop of Karnataka because most of the state lacks the cool temperate conditions needed for conventional apple production.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which crop is associated with sericulture in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Sericulture is the rearing of silkworms and production of raw silk. Karnataka is one of India's leading silk-producing states. Mulberry is the primary host plant.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which districts are associated with grape cultivation in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Grapes are cultivated in Vijayapura and Bagalkote districts. Pomegranate is grown in northern dry districts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which districts are associated with ragi cultivation in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Ragi (finger millet) is a major crop of the southern plateau districts. Rice is important in coastal, Kaveri and irrigated belts; jowar in northern dry districts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which districts are associated with tur/red gram cultivation in Karnataka?

options.B: Kalaburagi, Bidar, Vijayapura and northern districts

questions.explanation: Tur/red gram is important in Kalaburagi, Bidar, Vijayapura and northern districts. Bengal gram is important in northern and central drylands.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which are major irrigation projects in Karnataka?

options.A: Upper Krishna, Tungabhadra, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Bhadra

questions.explanation: Upper Krishna, Tungabhadra, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Bhadra, Hemavati, Kabini, Harangi, KRS and Upper Bhadra are major projects in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is a command area?

options.B: Area intended to receive irrigation water from a particular project through canals and distribution systems

questions.explanation: A command area is the area intended to receive irrigation water from a particular project through canals and distribution systems. Irrigation potential created is the designed capacity; actual irrigated area may be lower.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Upper Krishna Project includes which reservoirs?
questions.explanation: The Upper Krishna Project includes Almatti (Lal Bahadur Shastri) Dam and Narayanapura (Basava Sagar) Dam for irrigation in northern Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Tungabhadra Project serves irrigation and power in which districts?
questions.explanation: Tungabhadra Project provides irrigation and power in Vijayanagara, Ballari, Koppal, Raichur and adjoining areas.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Ghataprabha Project benefits which districts?
questions.explanation: Ghataprabha Project benefits Belagavi and Bagalkote command areas.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Malaprabha Project benefits which districts?
questions.explanation: Malaprabha Project (Navilaitirha/Renuka Sagar) provides irrigation in north Karnataka, mainly Belagavi and Bagalkote.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Upper Bhadra project is intended to benefit which type of districts?
questions.explanation: Upper Bhadra is a major lift-irrigation project intended to benefit drought-prone central districts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Yettinahole project is associated with:

options.B: Inter-basin drinking-water supply for drought-prone eastern districts

questions.explanation: Yettinahole is a proposed/inter-basin drinking-water supply scheme for drought-prone eastern districts. Its components, completion and operational status should be checked from current government releases.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Why is micro-irrigation important in Karnataka?

options.B: It improves application efficiency, reduces conveyance losses and supports water productivity
options.C: It is only for plantation crops

questions.explanation: Drip and sprinkler systems can improve application efficiency, reduce conveyance losses and support water productivity, especially in water-scarce districts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Why is Karnataka mineral-rich?

options.B: Because it lies on the ancient Dharwar craton with greenstone belts and iron-rich formations
options.D: Because of volcanic activity in the Deccan Traps

questions.explanation: Karnataka lies on the ancient Dharwar craton, containing greenstone belts and iron-rich formations, gold-bearing quartz reefs and diverse crystalline rocks.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is the major iron ore belt of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Ballari-Hospet-Sandur belt is a major iron ore-producing region in eastern Karnataka, associated with the Sandur schist belt.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Hutti Gold Mines are located in which district?
questions.explanation: Hutti Gold Mines in Raichur district is an important operating gold-mining centre.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Kolar Gold Fields mines were closed in which year?
questions.explanation: Kolar Gold Fields (KGF) in Kolar district is a historic gold-mining centre whose mines were closed in 2001.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which districts are associated with limestone deposits in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Limestone deposits are found in Kalaburagi, Bagalkote, Vijayapura, Belagavi and other districts, supporting cement and lime industries.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which mineral is associated with steel alloying and found in Ballari, Sandur and Shivamogga belts?
questions.explanation: Manganese is found in Ballari, Sandur, Shivamogga and other belts and is used in steel alloying.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Bauxite occurrences in Karnataka are ecologically sensitive because they are located in:

options.B: Selected Western Ghats / plateau occurrences, including Belagavi region

questions.explanation: Bauxite occurs in selected Western Ghats / plateau occurrences, including the Belagavi region. These locations are ecologically sensitive.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What environmental problems are associated with mining in Karnataka?

options.B: Deforestation, overburden dumps, soil erosion, dust, groundwater contamination, habitat fragmentation

questions.explanation: Deforestation, overburden dumps, soil erosion, dust, noise, groundwater contamination, altered drainage, habitat fragmentation and abandoned mine pits are major impacts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which city is the leading IT, aerospace, electronics and biotechnology hub of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru is the leading IT, aerospace, electronics, biotechnology, machine-tool and startup hub of Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Mangaluru is known for which industries?

options.B: Refining, petrochemicals, fertilisers, port logistics, fisheries and food processing

questions.explanation: Mangaluru has port-based, petrochemical, fertilizer and refinery-related industries along with fisheries and food processing.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Belagavi is known for which industries?

options.B: Foundry, machine tools, aerospace components, engineering and sugar

questions.explanation: Belagavi has foundry, machine tools, aerospace components, engineering and sugar industries.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Ballari-Hosapete-Sandur region is known for which industries?

options.B: Iron ore, steel, sponge iron and power

questions.explanation: Ballari-Hosapete-Sandur is known for iron ore, steel, sponge iron and power industries.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Plant (VISL) is located at:
questions.explanation: Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Plant (VISL) is located at Bhadravati in Shivamogga district, historically associated with iron and steel production and Sir M. Visvesvaraya.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: JSW Steel's Vijayanagar Works is located at:
questions.explanation: The integrated steel plant at Toranagallu in Ballari district is associated with JSW Steel's Vijayanagar Works, supported by the Ballari-Hospet iron ore belt.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Cement plants in Karnataka are concentrated in which limestone-rich areas?
questions.explanation: Cement plants are concentrated in limestone-rich areas such as Kalaburagi, Bagalkote and Vijayapura.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Sugar factories in Karnataka are important in which districts?

options.B: Belagavi, Bagalkote, Mandya and other cane-growing districts

questions.explanation: Sugar factories are important in Belagavi, Bagalkote, Mandya and other cane-growing districts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which railway zone is headquartered at Hubballi and serves a large part of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: South Western Railway (SWR), headquartered at Hubballi, serves a large part of Karnataka through divisions including Bengaluru, Mysuru and Hubballi.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Konkan Railway serves which region of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Konkan Railway is a major coastal railway route serving stations such as Karwar, Gokarna Road, Kumta, Honnavar, Bhatkal, Kundapura, Udupi and the Mangaluru region.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which metro rail operates in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Namma Metro operates in Bengaluru. It is managed by Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL).

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is the major international airport of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru is the major international airport. Other important airports include Mangaluru International Airport, Hubballi Airport, Belagavi Airport, Mysuru Airport and Kalaburagi Airport.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What was Karnataka's population as per Census 2011?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 recorded 61,095,297 people (about 6.11 crore) in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What was Karnataka's population density as per Census 2011?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 recorded a population density of 319 persons per km² for Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What was Karnataka's sex ratio as per Census 2011?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 recorded a sex ratio of 973 females per 1,000 males in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What was Karnataka's literacy rate as per Census 2011?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 recorded a literacy rate of 75.36% for Karnataka (male 82.47%; female 68.08%).

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What was Karnataka's urban population share as per Census 2011?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 recorded an urban population share of about 38.67% for Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which district was the most populous in Karnataka as per Census 2011?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru Urban was the most populous district in Census 2011, followed by Belagavi and Mysuru in the then district configuration.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the difference between sex ratio and child sex ratio?

options.B: Sex ratio is females per 1,000 males in total population; child sex ratio is girls per 1,000 boys in 0-6 age group
options.C: Sex ratio is for adults only
options.D: Child sex ratio is for all children under 18

questions.explanation: Sex ratio is the number of females per 1,000 males in the population. Child sex ratio is the number of girls per 1,000 boys in the 0-6 age group. They are separate indicators.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the difference between urban population and urban agglomeration?

options.B: Urban area is a statutory town or census town; urban agglomeration is a continuous urban spread including outgrowths or contiguous towns
options.C: Urban agglomeration is smaller than urban area
options.D: Urban population only counts city residents

questions.explanation: An urban area is a statutory town or census town under Census criteria. An urban agglomeration is a continuous urban spread comprising a town and adjoining outgrowths or contiguous towns meeting the Census definition.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is the capital and largest metropolitan centre of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru is Karnataka's capital and largest metropolitan centre, located on the southeastern Deccan Plateau.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are key urban environmental issues in Karnataka?

options.B: Traffic congestion, air pollution, urban heat islands, loss of lakes, groundwater depletion, flooding, solid-waste management

questions.explanation: Traffic congestion, air pollution, urban heat islands, loss of lakes and wetlands, groundwater depletion, flooding from encroached drains, solid-waste management, sewage discharge and peri-urban land conversion are major concerns.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Raichur Thermal Power Station is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Raichur Thermal Power Station (RTPS) is a coal-based thermal power station at Shaktinagar in Raichur district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Pavagada Solar Park is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Pavagada Solar Park is in Tumakuru district and is also called Shakti Sthala.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Kaiga Generating Station is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Kaiga Generating Station is a nuclear power station in Uttara Kannada district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Varahi hydroelectric project is located in which region?
questions.explanation: Varahi hydroelectric project is an underground hydroelectric station in the Varahi basin, Shivamogga region.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is the difference between renewable and non-renewable energy?

options.B: Renewable sources are replenished naturally; non-renewable sources are finite mineral resources

questions.explanation: Renewable sources are replenished naturally on human timescales (solar, wind, hydropower, sustainable biomass). Non-renewable sources such as coal, oil, gas and uranium are finite mineral resources.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Is nuclear energy classified as renewable?

options.B: No, it uses a finite fuel and is not classified as renewable

questions.explanation: Nuclear energy is low-carbon in operation but uses a finite fuel (uranium) and is not classified as renewable.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which regions of Karnataka are most drought-prone?
questions.explanation: Drought is concentrated in North Interior and rain-shadow districts due to rainfall variability, high demand and groundwater dependence.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Landslides in Karnataka are concentrated in which region?
questions.explanation: Landslides occur in steep Western Ghats and Malnad due to intense rain, slope cutting, road works and land-use change.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Why is the Western Ghats ecologically sensitive?

options.B: Because of high endemism, steep slopes, heavy rainfall, fragile soils, headwaters and connected forest habitats

questions.explanation: The Ghats combine high endemism, steep slopes, heavy rainfall, fragile soils, headwaters and connected forest habitats. Disturbance can trigger landslides, erosion, altered streamflow and biodiversity loss.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: How does climate change affect Karnataka?

options.B: Rising temperatures, changing monsoon, altered drought and flood risk, crop and forest stress, coastal sea-level rise

questions.explanation: Potential effects include rising average temperatures, more intense heat, changing monsoon timing and extremes, altered drought and flood risk, stress on crops and forests, coastal sea-level rise and shifts in species distribution.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What is sustainable development in the Karnataka context?

options.B: Integrating economic growth with water security, resilient agriculture, biodiversity protection, low-carbon energy and equitable access

questions.explanation: Sustainable development integrates economic growth with water security, resilient agriculture, biodiversity protection, low-carbon energy, sustainable mining, efficient cities, coastal management and equitable access to natural resources.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is the highest peak in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Mullayanagiri in Chikkamagaluru district, about 1,930 m, is the highest peak in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is the highest peak in Kodagu district?
questions.explanation: Tadiandamol is the highest peak in Kodagu district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is the largest major river basin in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Krishna basin is the largest major river basin in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is the best-known waterfall of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Jog Falls on the Sharavathi River is the best-known major waterfall of Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is commonly cited as the highest waterfall in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Kunchikal Falls on the Varahi River is commonly cited as Karnataka's highest waterfall, though published height and ranking depend on measurement method and seasonal flow.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is the major port of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: New Mangalore Port at Panambur is the major port of Karnataka. Karwar and Belekeri are non-major port facilities.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is the major operating gold mine in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Hutti Gold Mines in Raichur district is the major operating gold mine. Kolar Gold Fields mines closed in 2001.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Kolar Gold Fields mines were closed in which year?
questions.explanation: Kolar Gold Fields (KGF) in Kolar district is a historic gold-mining centre whose mines were closed in 2001.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is the major iron ore belt of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Ballari-Hospet-Sandur is the major iron ore belt of Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Pavagada Solar Park is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Pavagada Solar Park is in Tumakuru district and is also called Shakti Sthala.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Kaiga nuclear station is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Kaiga Generating Station is in Uttara Kannada district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is the headquarters of Bagalkote district?
questions.explanation: Bagalkote is the headquarters of Bagalkote district. The district lies in Northern Maidan in the Krishna basin with black and red soils and semi-arid climate.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Badami and Aihole heritage landscape is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Badami-Aihole heritage landscape is in Bagalkote district, which also has limestone/cement resources and crops like jowar, pulses, sugarcane and grapes.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Daroji Sloth Bear Sanctuary is located near which district?
questions.explanation: Daroji Sloth Bear Sanctuary is near Ballari district. Ballari is in the eastern dry plateau with iron ore and steel belt.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Gokak Falls and Hidkal dam are located in which district?
questions.explanation: Gokak Falls and Hidkal dam are in Belagavi district, which also has foundries and engineering industries and crops like sugarcane, jowar and maize.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Devanahalli airport region is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru Rural district includes the Devanahalli airport region and has red loamy soils, semi-arid climate, and crops like ragi, maize and horticulture.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which river is associated with the Linganamakki reservoir?
questions.explanation: Linganamakki reservoir is on the Sharavathi River in Shivamogga district and is a major reservoir for Sharavathi hydropower.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Supa dam is on which river?
questions.explanation: Supa dam is on the Kali River in Joida taluk, Uttara Kannada, part of the Kali hydropower system.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Kadra and Kodasalli dams are on which river?
questions.explanation: Kadra and Kodasalli dams are on the Kali River in Uttara Kannada, part of the Kali hydropower system.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which river is associated with the Jog Falls and Linganamakki reservoir?
questions.explanation: Both Jog Falls and Linganamakki reservoir are on the Sharavathi River in Shivamogga district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which river is associated with the Shivanasamudra falls and an early hydroelectric station?
questions.explanation: Shivanasamudra falls is on the Kaveri River and has Gaganachukki and Bharachukki falls and an early hydroelectric station.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Gokak Falls is associated with which historic activity?
questions.explanation: Gokak Falls on the Ghataprabha River has a historic power-generation association.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which district is historically an important coconut market and sericulture centre?
questions.explanation: Ramanagara (now Bengaluru South) is historically an important coconut market and sericulture is important in Ramanagara/Bengaluru South, Kolar, Mandya and Mysuru.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which crop is Karnataka one of India's leading producers of, with Ramanagara historically important?
questions.explanation: Karnataka is one of India's leading silk-producing states, with Ramanagara historically an important coconut market and sericulture centre.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which forest product is regulated in Karnataka despite its heritage association?
questions.explanation: Sandalwood is strongly associated with Karnataka's heritage and forest economy, but its availability and trade are regulated.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which sanctuary is commonly called a bird sanctuary and is a Ramsar site in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary is a designated Ramsar wetland and commonly called a bird sanctuary.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which is an important elephant landscape and corridor in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Karnataka is part of the Nilgiri-Eastern Ghats elephant landscape. Important connected forests include Bandipur, Nagarahole, BRT, Cauvery, Bannerghatta and adjoining Tamil Nadu/Kerala forests.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: The Southern Maidan is characterized by:

options.A: Broad dry plateau with black soils
options.B: Undulating plateau, generally higher and more dissected than northern plains, with red loamy soils

questions.explanation: The Southern Maidan is an undulating plateau, generally higher and more dissected than northern plains, with granite-gneiss landscape, red loamy soils and patches of black soil. Crops include ragi, maize, pulses, groundnut and sugarcane in irrigated tracts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which crops are typical of the Southern Maidan?

options.B: Ragi, maize, pulses, groundnut, sugarcane in irrigated tracts

questions.explanation: Southern Maidan crops include ragi, maize, pulses, groundnut and sugarcane in irrigated tracts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which crops are typical of the Northern Maidan?
questions.explanation: Northern Maidan crops include jowar, tur, cotton, pulses and oilseeds, with black cotton soils extensive in basaltic tracts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which river is associated with the Bhadra dam?
questions.explanation: Bhadra Dam is on the Bhadra River at Lakkavalli in Chikkamagaluru district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which river is associated with the Harangi reservoir?
questions.explanation: Harangi reservoir is on the Harangi River in Kodagu district, part of the Kaveri basin.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which river is associated with the Kabini reservoir?
questions.explanation: Kabini reservoir is on the Kabini River near H D Kote in Mysuru district, part of the Kaveri basin.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which river is associated with the Hemavati/Gorur reservoir?
questions.explanation: Hemavati/Gorur reservoir is on the Hemavati River in Hassan district.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which crop is associated with the Ramanagara/Bengaluru South, Kolar, Mandya and Mysuru districts?
questions.explanation: Sericulture is important in Ramanagara/Bengaluru South, Kolar, Mandya and Mysuru. Karnataka is one of India's leading silk-producing states.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Davanagere-Shivamogga region is known for which industries?
questions.explanation: Davanagere-Shivamogga region is known for textiles, agro-processing, sugar and engineering.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Kalaburagi-Bagalkote region is known for which industries?

options.B: Cement, limestone-based industries, sugar and agro-processing

questions.explanation: Kalaburagi-Bagalkote region is known for cement, limestone-based industries, sugar and agro-processing.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: The Vedavathi (Hagari) river is part of which river system?
questions.explanation: Vedavathi (Hagari) is part of the Tungabhadra-Krishna system.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Markandeya river is a tributary of which river?
questions.explanation: Markandeya is a tributary of the Ghataprabha. Godchinamalaki Falls is on the Markandeya River.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: Which rivers drain parts of southeastern Karnataka towards Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Palar and Pennar drain parts of the southeastern plateau towards Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are the key responses to drought in Karnataka?

options.B: Watershed development, crop diversification, micro-irrigation, drought planning

questions.explanation: Key responses to drought include watershed development, crop diversification, micro-irrigation and drought planning.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are the key responses to floods in Karnataka?

options.B: Floodplain zoning, warning systems, drainage restoration, dam coordination

questions.explanation: Key responses to floods include floodplain zoning, warning systems, drainage restoration and dam coordination.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are the key responses to soil erosion/desertification in Karnataka?

options.B: Contour bunding, cover crops, restoration, controlled grazing

questions.explanation: Key responses to soil erosion/desertification include contour bunding, cover crops, restoration and controlled grazing.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are the key responses to deforestation/fragmentation in Karnataka?

options.B: Protected areas, corridors, restoration and strict clearance compliance

questions.explanation: Key responses include protected areas, corridors, restoration and strict clearance compliance.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are the key responses to mining pollution in Karnataka?

options.B: Mine reclamation, dust control, monitoring and enforcement

questions.explanation: Key responses to mining pollution include mine reclamation, dust control, monitoring and enforcement.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are the key responses to river and lake pollution in Karnataka?

options.B: Sewage treatment, industrial effluent control, buffer protection

questions.explanation: Key responses to river and lake pollution include sewage treatment, industrial effluent control and buffer protection.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are the key responses to groundwater depletion in Karnataka?

options.B: Recharge, demand management, metering and efficient use

questions.explanation: Key responses to groundwater depletion include recharge, demand management, metering and efficient use.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are the key responses to coastal erosion in Karnataka?

options.B: Coastal sediment studies, nature-based protection, regulated development

questions.explanation: Key responses to coastal erosion include coastal sediment studies, nature-based protection and regulated development.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are the key responses to human-wildlife conflict in Karnataka?

options.B: Corridors, early warning, barriers where suitable, compensation and community measures

questions.explanation: Key responses to human-wildlife conflict include corridors, early warning, barriers where suitable, compensation and community measures.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are the key responses to heatwaves and air pollution in Karnataka?

options.B: Heat action plans, urban trees, clean transport and emissions control

questions.explanation: Key responses to heatwaves and air pollution include heat action plans, urban trees, clean transport and emissions control.

questions.subject: Karnataka Geography
questions.question: What are surface-water and groundwater resources?

options.A: Surface water is underground; groundwater is in rivers
options.B: Surface water includes rivers, streams, reservoirs, tanks, lakes and wetlands; groundwater is stored in weathered zones, fractures, joints, alluvium and sedimentary aquifers
